answer_1.quote: Machine translation (MT) has become a fundamental pillar of multilingual communication, enabling rapid and scalable information transfer across languages.
answer_1.outputs: The paper focuses on evaluating machine translation outputs through iterative translation processes and degradation-aware scoring, with applications in low-resource and long-form translation scenarios.

answer_2.quote: We compute raw scores q (j) i using an automatic metric (xCOMET), and aim to transform them into context-aware scores r (j) i.

answer_4.quote: We compare our telephone-supervised evaluation models to existing metrics using WMT MQM human annotations.
answer_4.guideline: The evaluation uses human-annotated MQM scores and Direct Assessment (DA) scores from WMT, which involve human judgments on translation quality, including error severity and adequacy.
